source: CAMFAD student thesis: "Establishment of a New Coconut Plantation Farm", National School of Agriculture, July 1994
text:
Three insect/mite pests of coconut are profiled with scientific names and control recommendations:

Tetranychus telarius (a spider mite): reddish/orange colored mite found on the leaves. Control: spray Binapacryl, Dicofol, or Dimethoate (use one of these), applied as soon as the pest first appears on the crop.

Coelaenomenodera elaidis (a leaf-mining beetle/leafminer): found mining within coconut leaves. Control: spray Gamma-BHC or Malathion (use one of these), applied once the pest population has built up to a noticeable/dense level.

Oryctes monoceros (rhinoceros beetle): attacks and damages the growing bud (crown) and stem of the palm; if it damages the growing point severely, it can kill the tree outright or severely stunt future growth. No highly effective chemical control is noted; the recommended approach is prevention through sanitation — removing and not allowing organic waste, rotting plant material, and debris piles to accumulate in or around the plantation, since these serve as breeding sites for the beetle's grubs. Keeping the farm clean is described as the main defense against this pest.
